Josour for Windows and macOS · Phase 4 of 4 · verification

Desktop redesign: what was built and how it was checked

The desktop app now runs on the qantara identity approved in Phase 1 and drawn in Phase 2. This page shows each window before and after, the states that are new, the generated icons, the test and build results, and an explicit list of what was not verified on real hardware. Nothing is committed.

What changed

AreaChange
Tokens and generatordocs/design/brand-tokens.json (replaces mobile-tokens.json); scripts/brand-theme.py (replaces mobile-theme.py) writes Josour.Brand/Theme/Tokens.axaml, both apps' Theme/Metrics.axaml, the desktop FluentOverrides.axaml, BrandGeometry.g.cs, the Android resources and every desktop image, with a stamp for --check.
Josour.Brand (new)Tokens, Readex Pro + OFL, BrandFonts, BrandMotion, BrandLockup, Motif, Icon (with the desktop's added kinds). The phone now references it; one XAML namespace serves brand and app controls.
Desktop themeApp.axaml follows the system theme; Theme/Styles.axaml, Theme/Controls.axaml (Card, InfoBar on tokens), DesktopTheme (type scale per language), PlatformButtonRow (each system's button order). The Fluent icon set and the old typography/opacity styles are gone.
ScreensEvery window rewritten on the components: main window (app bar, status hero, Contacts and This device tabs, in-window confirmations), request, sign-in, first run, settings, about, user management, licences (now with the font licence). Start-up failure names the real log folder.
View modelsHostStatus + grace + ranked Notices; MainViewModel.Hero, tray state, reconnect, sign-out and quit confirmations; request expiry state and AcceptText; contact trust confirmation, loading and error state; sign-out notice and password reveal; admin disable confirmation and loading.
Tray, menus, notificationsIcons per state and taskbar theme (registry read, Windows), template images on macOS, a state line at the top of the menu, User management only for administrators, Exit and ⌘Q ask first while sharing, a macOS app menu. The request toast's third line is the plain consequence.
Packagingpublish-app.sh copies the generated .icns after --check (no more upscaling the 64-px .ico); publish-exe.ps1 and CI run --check; Inno Setup gets SetupIconFile and the wizard images; NOTICE says the font ships in the desktop apps.
Strings20 new Desktop* keys, 8 desktop-only edits, 33 phone keys reused unchanged. No shared value changed, so the phone's wording is untouched.

Not verified on real hardware

Everything above ran headless on this Mac, without launching the real app (this Mac has a real install signed in to production). These need a person on a real machine:

  • Real Windows 10 and 11: the window frame and title bar in both themes, DPI at 100, 150 and 200 % (only rasterised at 2× here), Readex Pro through DirectWrite.
  • The Windows tray: the four icons on a real taskbar in light and dark, the switch when the taskbar theme changes while the app runs, and the native menu.
  • Windows toasts: the new icon through the toast registration (an old registration may keep the old icon until it is re-registered), the new third line.
  • The installer: Inno Setup compiling with the new SetupIconFile and wizard images (not built on this Mac).
  • Narrator and VoiceOver: the accessible names, the live announcements of the hero and dialogs, focus on the request heading.
  • The macOS menu bar on a real Mac: the template image size and tint, whether a click opens the menu, the app menu (and whether Avalonia adds its own items to it), ⌘, ⌘W ⌘Q.
  • The .icns in Finder and the Dock (written directly, not through iconutil).
  • Mica: not used (decision 8), nothing to verify.
  • Keyboard: tab order and the focus ring on a real keyboard.

## Unreleased

### Windows and macOS
- **A new look around the qantara mark.** The desktop app is rebuilt on the identity the phone got in 2.6.0
  ([docs/design/desktop-phase1-foundation.html](docs/design/desktop-phase1-foundation.html), mockups in
  [desktop-phase2-mockups.html](docs/design/desktop-phase2-mockups.html)): Readex Pro for Arabic and English, the teal
  and ink colours with light and dark themes that follow the system while the app runs, the lock-up on sign-in, first run
  and About, and new icons generated from the logo: the app icon (a white symbol on a teal plate, in the `.ico` and in
  Apple's `.icns` grid), the installer's art, and a tray and menu-bar icon that shows the state in four shapes (available,
  not available, can't reach the server, in a session). On macOS the menu-bar icon is a template image the system tints.
- **The main window answers one question first**: can a request reach this computer now, and if not, what to do. A status
  hero with the Available switch sits above two tabs, Contacts and This device; a short reconnect reads as "getting
  ready", and the firewall, VPN and simulated-server warnings are ranked instead of stacked. During a session the hero
  shows who, the time left, the data used and "End the session now". The bottom status strip is gone: Settings, About and
  User management are in the ⋯ menu on Windows and in the app menu on macOS.
- **Consent is fairer.** Accept and Reject on a request have the same weight, in each system's order, and come after
  "What accepting means" in plain words; ticking "always allow" renames Accept to "Accept and always allow"; an expired
  request says so instead of vanishing; turning on "without asking" for a contact asks first; signing out, quitting
  while sharing and disabling an account ask first and say what stops.
- Sign-in shows why the server signed this device out, and the password can be shown. Each system's shortcuts:
  Ctrl/⌘ , for Settings, Ctrl/⌘ W to close the main window to the tray or menu bar, ⌘Q to quit on macOS, and Esc to
  cancel a dialog. Every icon button and switch has an accessible name.
- The theme files and brand images of both apps are generated from one tokens file (`docs/design/brand-tokens.json`) and
  the logo by `scripts/brand-theme.py`; the publish scripts and CI check that they are current. The identity shared by the
  phone and the desktop (tokens, font, lock-up, motif, icons) is one project, `Josour.Brand`.

Commit message

feat(desktop): redesign the Windows and macOS app around the qantara mark

Rebuild the desktop app on the identity the phone got in 2.6.0, following the
approved foundation and mockups in docs/design/desktop-phase1-foundation.html
and desktop-phase2-mockups.html:

- One source of truth for both apps: docs/design/brand-tokens.json (the
  phone's tokens plus the desktop's density) and scripts/brand-theme.py,
  which replaces mobile-theme.py and also generates the desktop theme, the
  .ico, the .icns, the tray and menu-bar icons in four states and the
  installer art. --check needs only Python; the publish scripts and CI run it.
- Josour.Brand, a shared project: tokens, Readex Pro, the logo geometry and
  the lock-up, motif and icon controls, moved from the phone (its tests and
  APK build unchanged in behaviour).
- Desktop: Readex Pro, light and dark following the system, a status hero
  above two tabs (Contacts, This device) instead of the bottom strip, ranked
  warnings, the session in the hero, equal Accept/Reject in each system's
  order with the consequence in plain words, confirmation before trusting a
  contact, signing out, quitting while sharing and disabling an account, an
  expired request that says so, the sign-out reason on sign-in, a password
  reveal, Ctrl/Cmd shortcuts and a macOS app menu, accessible names on icon
  buttons and switches.
- View-model additions only (HostStatus with a 5 s grace, ranked notices,
  hero and tray state, confirmations); no networking or protocol change.
- Copy: 20 new Desktop* keys, 8 desktop-only edits, 33 phone keys reused;
  no shared value changes.

Headless Skia tests draw 39 window states in Arabic and English, light and
dark and at 2x, and fail on cut-off text; behaviour tests cover each
view-model addition.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Follow-ups (out of scope, not done)

  • macOS notifications as Josour need a signed bundle and UNUserNotificationCenter (ADR-0011); today they still show as Script Editor.
  • About 50 strings the desktop no longer shows (the Phase 1 leftovers and the keys retired here) can be removed once the phone is checked not to read them.
  • The phone's Mobile* keys now read by the desktop could get neutral names in a later cleanup (touches the phone).
  • The web admin dashboard (favicon, header) and the README and docs screenshots are still on the old identity.
  • The installer is English only.
